citation.authors: Mahmoud BH, Ruvolo E, Hexsel CL, Liu Y et al

record.finding: In normal lower-back skin of 20 volunteers, visible light induced darker and more sustained pigmentation than UVA1 in skin types IV-VI. Existing marks were not tested.

record.population: 20 volunteers with skin types IV-VI, plus skin type II for comparison
record.design: Controlled irradiation of the lower back with long-wave UVA1 or visible light, 7 time points over two weeks
record.finding: Both UVA1 and visible light induced pigmentation in skin types IV-VI. Pigmentation from visible light was darker and more sustained. No pigmentation was seen in skin type II.
record.note: Funding not stated in the abstract; funding not checked. Normal skin, not existing marks (fact-check 12 Nov). Tests what light does to skin; it does not test whether any sunscreen prevents it.
